nodes.label: Fn_Specs — Editorial Gate Features FR-01..FR-05
nodes.description: Functional specification for the five editorial gates. Covers intake, validation and investigation as two distinct transitions, drafting with meaning-invariance, Line 2 human review at T5 with a blind first pass, and independence classification with three outcomes and no silent fourth state. Its section 9 applies the D-30 redundancy filter and names five components that require SPECS.

nodes.label: Fn_Specs — Publication Feature Group FR-09, FR-10, FR-13
nodes.description: Functional specification for publishing, confirming a manual publish, and order-driven retraction. Grouped because a retraction is a publication and a notice inherits its targets from the original, so FR-13 cannot function without FR-09's target model. First spec written to the merged structure adding User Stories and Risks.

nodes.label: T1 Execution Runbook
nodes.description: Step-by-step procedure for all 23 T1 items, fulfilling D-21. Orders the four-payload CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md edit first as highest leverage, then verification apparatus, ratification, wording fixes, governance placement, the decision batch, and Fn_Specs. Carries the standing constraint to apply proposed text in full, which is the G32 countermeasure.

nodes.label: Intent Hierarchy (D-29)
nodes.description: PRD to Modular_PRD to Fn_Specs to SPECS. Intent flows downward; each tier elaborates the one above and may never contradict it. Change localization is the purpose: a change lands in the tier that owns it and only that document changes.

nodes.label: SPECS Redundancy Rule (D-30)
nodes.description: If a behaviour can be defined clearly enough in Fn_Specs, a SPECS document for it is redundant and must not be written. SPECS exists only where functional definition alone cannot determine implementation. This prevents SPECS becoming a restatement layer, which is the mechanism behind the project's recurring drift defect.

nodes.label: Spec Tier Mapping (D-34)
nodes.description: The specs-creator tool chain is a labelling map, not a blocker. app-vision.md maps to Modular_PRD because an app is a product; prd.md maps to docs/fn-specs; tech-specs.md maps to docs/specs; ux.md maps to docs/specs/ux for UI/UX per tech-stack. A stack change lands in specs and neither disturbs fn-specs.

nodes.label: Two Progress Trackers (D-35)
nodes.description: Modular_PRD section 8.0 tracks build versions and their sprints; the Alpha Portfolio plan tracks projects. A sprint stays inside one project and a new project is a portfolio event, so the two trackers do not overlap. Notation is mandatory: V1 and V2 are build versions, 1.7 and 1.8 are document revision lineage, and they are unrelated.

nodes.label: Tracking Files versus Specs (D-36)
nodes.description: V1-*.md are tracking files that freeze at sprint close; specs carry no version prefix and never freeze. Specs moved out of the version-named directory so separation is by lifecycle rather than version. Each spec section is marked with the build version that introduced it, and an unmarked change to a V1 section is a defect rather than an update.

nodes.label: Plan Pack Reclassification (D-37)
nodes.description: DATA_MODEL, ARCHITECTURE and TASKS came from the original Q&A flow alongside PRD.md and are frozen candidate references of the same status class. D5's claim that they were generated from the app name is not supportable: they name the exact six gate roles, the full five-gate flow, and the correct provisioned stack. Accurate about the substrate, silent on governance rather than wrong about it.

nodes.label: Topic Semantics (D-38)
nodes.description: In an editorial business the topic is the subject, not a label. articles.topic_id is a single foreign key holding exactly one subject topic; trend_signals with signal_type topic_tag hold many analytical tags for trending and angle analysis. Two concepts sharing one word. The schema is correct as applied; FR-01's wording conflates them.

nodes.label: One Word, Two Concepts — Recurring Error Pattern
nodes.description: Five recorded instances of a naming difference being mistaken for a structural incompatibility: Project versus Product PRD, app-vision.md versus Modular_PRD, pub_target versus platform_type, tracking files versus specs, and subject topic versus analytical tag. Countermeasure: before recording a contradiction, check what the unfamiliar label maps to and whether one word is carrying two concepts. D-22's dual financial terminology is the precedent.
